national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today lauded the successful conclusion of BRICS Summit 2026 in New Delhi, saying that the world saw the strong convening power of India, as most of the heads of state were present to represent their countries. Talking to the media, Dr Jaishankar said that it is important to recognise that this BRICS summit was taking place in a very polarised world, where there are two major conflicts and very strong opinions and interests. He said that all countries were able to get out a statement urging peace, security, stability, long-term understanding, the smooth flow of global trade, supply chains, energy, and of the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. Dr Jaishankar informed that there were 32 delegations that had come from 11 member states, 10 partner states, four regional organisations and seven international organisations. He said that, even in the midst of this polarisation, a consensus was forged on the toughest issue of the day, which was the West Asia conflict. The Minister stated that the BRICS countries were very clear that any act of terrorism is a criminal act, and it also explicitly recognised the unacceptability of the Pahalgam attack. Condemning the terrorism, Dr Jaishankar said that BRICS emphasised zero tolerance for terrorism and rejected double standards in countering it.

Daily Excelsior 04:18 AM Sep 15, 2026 IST Journalists from Jammu posing for a group photograph during their Bhopal tour on Monday. Excelsior Correspondent BHOPAL, Sept 14: A 10-member media delegation from Jammu began a press tour of Madhya Pradesh with visits to two of the state's important archaeological and cultural heritage sites, the historic Siva Temple at Bhojpur and the prehistoric rock shelters of Bhimbetka. On the first day of the tour, the journalists visited the Siva Temple at Bhojpur, where they were briefed by officials accompanying the delegation on the history and architectural significance of the monument. Advertisement The delegation was also briefed on the temple's unique architectural features, including its massive stone construction and the scale of the structure. Officials explained the historical importance of the site and efforts to preserve the monument as part of the region's archaeological heritage. The journalists later proceeded to Bhimbetka, one of India's most important prehistoric archaeological sites and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Officials explained that the archaeological evidence at Bhimbetka spans a very long period of human history, with the site offering insights into the development of human culture and artistic expression. The delegation's visit to both sites provided the journalists with an opportunity to understand Madhya Pradesh's rich archaeological heritage beyond written accounts and photographs. The tour has been organized by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, to provide journalists with an opportunity to experience the cultural, historical and developmental landscape of Madhya Pradesh firsthand. national_raw_news.title: SKUAST‑K scholar brings national recognition at NBEC-2026, Bengaluru - Rising Kashmir
national_raw_news.content: SKUAST‑K scholar brings national recognition at NBEC-2026, Bengaluru Advertisment Breaking News City SKUAST‑K scholar brings national recognition at NBEC-2026, Bengaluru RK News 14 Sep 2026 07:30 IST Follow Us Srinagar, Sep 13: In a landmark achievement for SKUAST‑K, Bushra Naaz, PhD scholar under the mentorship of Dr. Ajaz Ahmed Malik, Head, KVK, Ganderbal has been declared a winner at the National Bio Entrepreneurship Competition (NBEC) 2026, held in Bengaluru. The 2026 edition received an overwhelming response, with over 3,200 registrations from 34 States and Union Territories, making it one of the most competitive national platforms for science-driven entrepreneurship. After successive rounds of screening, mentoring, pitching, and evaluation on parameters such as scientific validity, novelty, feasibility, business potential, team strength, and clarity of articulation, only the most promising student advanced to the Grand Finale. Her pioneering research on plant-based meat analogues stood out for its scientific depth, translational potential, and entrepreneurial promise. In recognition of this breakthrough, Bushra Naaz received a ₹1 lakh award, presented in the presence of Dr. Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, Executive Chairperson of Biocon, and other eminent figures from India’s biotechnology ecosystem. Reflecting on the achievement, Dr. Ajaz Ahmed Malik, Head KVK, Ganderbal and Major Advisor to Bushra Naaz, remarked. The recognition of this work is deeply gratifying. For over a decade, I have been engaged with the scientific potential of fava bean, and it is inspiring to see this line of research now being advanced by my student into an innovative solution with societal and commercial relevance. Vice Chancellor SKUAST-K Prof. Nazir Ahmad Ganai congratulated both Bushra Naaz and Dr. Ajaz Malik, stating: This achievement is a proud moment for SKUAST‑K and aligns with our vision to be counted among the top universities in the country. It exemplifies how our scholars and faculty are not only contributing to academic excellence but also translating research into innovation and entrepreneurship.
